DaVita duopoly competition in the U.S. and labor-cost pressure across the clinic network; recurring special items (FME25+ program, portfolio optimization, China exit charge of about EUR 110M expected Q3 2026)

analysis_md:
# FMS — Fresenius Medical Care AG

v5.4 run, 2026-10-18. 20-F filer (FY2025 Form 20-F filed 2026-02-24), reporting currency EUR, converted to USD by the engine. Price $22.17 per ADS (nasdaq_quote_api). All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or segments.json — none are recomputed.

**Scope note:** the engine's market_cap_est is $6,455,695,048 — that multiplies the per-ADS price by the ordinary share count, so it understates the true market cap by the 2x ADS factor (one ADS = 1/2 ordinary share; the ordinary-share equivalent price is about twice the ADS price). The true cap is therefore roughly $12.9B — under the $40B scope limit on either basis, so in_scope_under_40b is true and nothing in the scoring turns on it.

## What it is
The world's leading provider of products and services for people with kidney disease (20-F Item 4.B, via profile.json): Care Delivery — about 3,513 dialysis clinics treating about 290,000 patients; Care Enablement — the dialysis machines, dialyzers and products the clinics (and competitors) consume, including the 5008X high-volume hemodiafiltration system rolling out in the U.S.; Value-Based Care — capitated kidney-care contracts. FY2025 segment revenue (segments.json, EUR): Care Delivery €13,238,321,000 (67.5% of total, −2.1% YoY), Care Enablement €4,141,908,000 (21.1%, +2.0%), Value-Based Care €2,247,373,000 (11.5%, +28.2%). FY2025 revenue €19,628M as filed (fundamentals.json), +1.5% in EUR (+5.4% at constant currency per the company's FY2025 release).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (20-F via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv, USD-converted):** operating cash flow $3,150,173,825; capex $1,075,125,000 — by override, see OVERRIDES; SBC $11,750,000 — by override, see OVERRIDES.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $2,063,298,825 = $7.09 per ordinary share = $3.54 per ADS** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_latest_per_share $3.5429 per ADS).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $3,105,063,933 total for FY2025 — above the conservative figure, mainly because the working-capital term is a release; the OCF-based conservative figure is the one used throughout.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (dcf_numbers.json: oe_positive_years_of_last_5 "5/5"). Net debt $6,684,302,400 (basis: LongtermBorrowings + CurrentPortionOfLongtermBorrowings) = 7.10x normalized OE — see HIGH_NET_DEBT below. The engine's net debt carries no lease liabilities (lease_liabilities_latest is null), so total fixed obligations are higher than the 7.10x figure suggests.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base, the median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $3.2328 per ADS** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). Per-ADS bases by year on the override basis: the median sits between the FY2024 and FY2025 per-ADS figures (latest FY $3.5429). No TTM pin: ttm.py reads us-gaap only and does not run for this IFRS filer (WORKER_SPEC step 4), so the median base is used and the interim 2026 evidence is handled under STALE_FY below.
- The base is conservative by construction: the capex override charges the FY2025 filed capex (€915M) to FY2023 and FY2024 as well, whose filed capex was €685M and €699M — the median year (FY2023) is charged about €230M more capex than it filed. A year-by-year filing-true base would be higher; the override base is the floor, not the midpoint.

## OVERRIDES — the preliminary run was DATA_GAP on three fields plus the ADS ratio
The preliminary engine run emitted no tier: `data_gap: [sbc, capex, shares]` for FY2023–2025 plus ADS_RATIO_MISSING. All four were resolved within the bounded authority (WORKER_SPEC step 8); every override check in the final dcf_numbers.json reports out_of_band: false.
- **ads_ratio 0.5 (filing):** one ADS represents 1/2 of an ordinary share — FY2025 20-F Item 9 (p. 147): the two-for-one ADS split effective December 3, 2012 changed the ratio to two ADSs representing one share (depositary: Bank of New York Mellon); the same 1/2 ratio is carried in the NYSE-registered ADS class title. Per-share figures are scaled x0.5 so they are comparable to the $22.17 ADS price (flag ADS_RATIO_APPLIED).
- **capex_override €915,000,000 (kind "filing"):** the engine's PPE capex tags carry no value from FY2020 onward in companyfacts (last filed FY2019 €1,124,791,000, statements.json), while the filer's own consolidated cash-flow statement reports "Purchases of property, plant and equipment and capitalized development costs" every year: €685M (FY2023), €699M (FY2024), €915M (FY2025). The single-value override uses the latest filed year for every missing period (filled 2020-12-31 through 2025-12-31) — 0.81x the last engine-filed value, in band, and conservative for FY2023/24 as noted above.
- **sbc_override €10,000,000 (kind "estimate"):** no SBC line is filed in the cash-flow statement / companyfacts for FY2020–2025 under any engine tag (statements.json: SBC blank FY2020–2025), so the engine's SBC leg gaps even though the 20-F discloses the expense in Note 23 "Share-based plans": total share-based compensation expense, by component sum (no total is printed), was €45,124,000 (FY2025) / €38,458,000 (FY2024) / €32,515,000 (FY2023). Most of that is NOT the leg the OE template subtracts: the legacy plans (LTIP 2024+, LTIP 2022+, MB LTIP 2020, LTIP 2019, MB LTIP 2019) are cash-settled ("In cash") — a cash personnel cost already borne inside operating cash flow — and only the new plans (LTIP 2025+, MB LTIP 2024+) can be equity-settled. The equity-settled expense — the non-cash leg the template targets — was €8,371,000 in FY2025 (LTIP 2025+ €6,293,000 + MB LTIP 2024+ €2,078,000) and nil in FY2024/FY2023. The €10M override is that filing figure rounded up, applied flat (overstating FY2023/24, so conservative); it is 5.02x the last engine-filed SBC value (FY2019 €1,992,000, inside the 0.1x–10x band) and about 0.5% of the gated years' OE — immaterial to the base and the tier either way, and used instead of a silent zero.
- **shares_override 291,190,575 (kind "filing"):** diluted shares are missing in companyfacts for FY2023–2025 (in fact all years) — only the basic weighted-average count is tagged. The filer's own Note 22 EPS reconciliation (FY2025 20-F) shows why there is no separate diluted count to file: "Weighted average number of shares outstanding" 291,190,575 for FY2025 and 293,413,449 for FY2024/FY2023, "Potentially dilutive shares" nil in all three years, and basic EPS = diluted EPS (€3.36 / €1.83 / €1.70, identical on the face of the income statement). The filed FY2025 count is therefore the filer's own diluted denominator. It replaces counts that differ by <1% in the gated years.
- **Measured impact (dcf_numbers.json override_impact, engine-native median base):** zero-fill base $4.9501/ADS → final $3.2328/ADS; zero-fill weighted IRR 26.26% → final weighted IRR 18.14%. The overrides are the only reason a tier exists (unblocks_tier) and they move the verdict DOWN by about 8.1pp of IRR — the v4-style zero-fill run would have printed a fake Tier A.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: World's leading dialysis provider (about 3,513 clinics, about 290,000 patients, 20-F Item 4.B) with vertical integration into machines/dialyzers (Care Enablement) and unmatched clinic scale — but a reimbursement price-taker in a DaVita duopoly, with ROIC proxy down from 13.6% (2018) to 4.6% (2023/24) recovering to 7.2% (2025) and gross margin down from 33.9% to 25.6%, so the measured franchise earns around its cost of capital, not well above it.
- FOR: world's largest dialysis provider — clinic density and purchasing scale no challenger can replicate quickly; vertically integrated Care Enablement (machines/dialyzers, incl. the 5008X, first FDA-cleared high-volume hemodiafiltration system in the U.S.) feeding its own clinics; life-sustaining, non-discretionary recurring treatments with the global dialysis population growing about 4–5%/yr (20-F Item 4.B); Value-Based Care scaling fast (+28.2% FY2025 segment revenue) on the clinic network and nephrologist relationships.
- AGAINST: reimbursement price-taker — U.S. Medicare/commercial rates are set by payors; measured returns do not show a wide moat (ROIC proxy, fundamentals.json: 9.1% 2016, 10.6% 2017, 13.6% 2018, 8.3% 2019, 8.9% 2020, 6.8% 2021, 4.9% 2022, 4.6% 2023, 4.6% 2024, 7.2% 2025; gross margin 33.9% in 2016 → 24.6% in 2024 → 25.6% in 2025); U.S. same-market treatment growth was −0.9% in Q2 2026 — growth is rate/mix and Value-Based Care, not treatments; DaVita duopoly competition and clinic labor-cost pressure; recurring special items (FME25+ program, portfolio optimization, a China peritoneal-dialysis exit charge of about €110M expected in Q3 2026).
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection. A moat above 5 is not available on this evidence: the rubric's 7+ requires ROIC well above the cost of capital through a cycle, and FMS printed 4.6% in both 2023 and 2024.

## DCF — v5.4 final run (2026-10-18)
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** the engine blend is 4.18% (rev CAGR 5y 1.03%, rev CAGR 3y 3.68%, latest revenue YoY 14.81%, OE/share CAGR 2y 4.68%). The 14.81% "latest YoY" is a USD-translation artifact — FY2025 revenue grew +1.5% in EUR; the EUR/USD period-end rate moved from 1.0389 to 1.175. Real prints: FY2025 revenue +5.4% at constant currency, Q2 2026 revenue +4% cc / +5% organic, H1 2026 +3% cc, and 2026 guidance is broadly flat revenue with operating income within a mid-single-digit band at cc excluding special items. Default offsets (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp) would have started the bull at +9.18% and the super bull at +16.18% — above every revenue print the company has made — so offsets were recalibrated downward to −10/−4/0/+3/+7pp (starts −5.82% / +0.18% / +4.18% / +7.18% / +11.18%) with this written reason: the two bull starts are OE growth, not revenue growth, and are carried by operating leverage from the margin recovery already printing (operating income +31.2% in FY2025; Q2 2026 operating income excl. special items +20%, +23% at cc) plus FME25+ savings — if that recovery stalls, the bull cases fail, which is why probabilities were also skewed down (15/25/30/20/10: 40% on bear-or-worse for flat guidance, −0.9% U.S. treatment growth, 7.10x leverage and the October 2026 CEO transition). OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $22.17.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −5.8% | 0.75 | Rate cuts / volume decline compounds; deleveraging eats OE | $14.04 | 10.09% |
| Bear | 25% | +0.2% | 0.90 | Flat guidance is the reality; margin recovery stalls | $21.66 | 14.71% |

| Super bull | 10% | +11.2% | 1.25 | Full FME25+ delivery + 5008X adoption + VBC profitability | $47.46 | 27.49% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $27.88 (+25.8% vs price), IV@12% $36.88, IV@10% $46.90, IV@20% $19.77, IV@25% $15.29; weighted IRR 18.14%, base-case IRR 18.46%.**

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.56 months ago): no TTM pin is available — ttm.py reads us-gaap only and does not run for IFRS filers, so the median base stands, per WORKER_SPEC step 4. Interim evidence checked instead: H1 2026 (6-K results) revenue €9,473M (−2% reported, +3% cc) and Q2 2026 operating income excl. special items +20% YoY — no inflection that invalidates the FY2025-based median; the margin-recovery direction is, if anything, confirmed, and it is carried in the bull cases rather than the base.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): structural, not a one-off.
